problem: VLN agents such as ET on ALFRED tend to latch onto salient words like nouns, or ignore language and rely on vision, rather than grasping the deeper semantics of instructions. As a result they do poorly on navigation sub-tasks. The benefit of Computational Paninian Grammar (CPG) karaka relations has not been studied in multi-modal vision-and-language settings.
motivation: Karaka relations capture modifier-modified links between verbs and their arguments and sit closer to language semantics than Stanford dependencies. The authors believe that making the language encoder predict these relations would ground spatial relations in instructions better and raise navigation performance on ALFRED.
key_idea: Pre-train the language encoder of the Episodic Transformer (ET) to predict CPG karaka relations, then compare this against POS-, syntax-tree- and dependency-based pre-training on ALFRED.
insight: The paper is a proposal with no experiments or ablations, so it offers no empirical insight yet. The hypothesis is that explicit modifier-modified supervision in the language tower improves grounding of spatial relations and generalization.
method: Base model ET: Episodic Transformer, with separate language and visual encoders and a multimodal transformer encoder over concatenated embeddings, using the full history of observations and actions.
Karaka-based pre-training: the language encoder is pre-trained to explicitly predict CPG karaka relations from the instructions.
Baseline pre-training strategies: POS-based, syntax-tree-based and dependency-based language tower pre-training, used for comparison.
Planned analysis: ablations and studies of the generalization and interpretability of ET under each pre-training strategy.

setting.backbone: Episodic Transformer (ET), with a language encoder pre-trained on karaka annotations (planned)
setting.training_data: ALFRED, plus planned karaka/POS/syntax/dependency annotations for language pre-training; no details given
setting.observation: egocentric RGB visual observation history plus language instructions (ET on ALFRED)
setting.action_space: ALFRED discrete navigation and interaction actions

numbers_note: Proposal/plan paper; no experimental results reported.
results: No results are reported. The paper only outlines a planned study of karaka-based pre-training of ET's language encoder on ALFRED.
limitations: No experiments or quantitative results; the study is only proposed.
Restricted to ALFRED and the ET model, with no details on annotation generation for English instructions.
